reason: This Hebrew text from 1 Samuel presents a narrative that culminates in Samuel (a judge/leader) addressing the Israelite people and reproaching their ingratitude. Samuel explicitly states that God delivered them from Egypt and numerous oppressors, yet they rejected God by demanding a human king. The passage subsequently shows Saul, the newly anointed king, being presented to an ungrateful people—many of whom (the 'sons of Belial' בְנֵ֧י בְלִיַּ֣עַל) despise him and refuse to honor him. The narrative perspective privileges the leaders' view of the people's ingratitude, particularly through Samuel's direct address to the assembly (וַיַּצְעֵ֤ק שְׁמוּאֵל...). While the text is third-person rather than first-person narration, it consistently frames events from the vantage point of leaders confronting popular rejection and ungratefulness.
